messages:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a same‑sku sweep (A100-40g) across aws/us-west-2, gcp/us-east1, gcp/eu-west1. same CUDA driver family but two builds (525.105 vs 525.89). eu-west1 p95 is ~8-12% higher than us-west2 consistently. anyone seen cross-region signal drift like this? logs attached to the ticket.

sara: can you paste the exact perf run and the launch config? interested in clocks/pstate and batching flags.

alex: sure — here's the core command and one failing snippet:
```bash
./run_bench --model redwood-7b --dtype=int8 --seq=512 --batch=1 --autobatch=on --warmup=100
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.gr,clocks.sm --format=csv
```
log excerpt:
```
[2026-02-12 14:02:03] p95=48.2ms (eu-west1) p95=44.4ms (us-west2)
[profile] gemm_kernel: fallback_generic_gemm int8 path used on node-7
```

mike_g: two quick suspects — (1) clock governor differences / pstate not enforced; (2) libcudnn/cuBLAS build differences that pick different kernels. providers sometimes ship slightly different firmware/microcode.

alex: we did set NVIDIA pstate to performance on boot, but I noticed `clock governor: schedutil` on GCP nodes vs `performance` on AWS. Also cuBLAS reported 11.10 on eu-west1 vs 11.11 on us-west2.

jia: that can definitely cause kernel selection variance. generic_gemm fallback for int8 is a tell — likely one of the optimized kernels couldn't be used due to a missing symbol or different CUDA ABI. also check THP/NUMA interleaving and iommu settings, they can affect memcpy latencies for large KV cache hits.

alex: tried forcing clocks via nvidia-smi and disabling autoscaling of clocks. ran with `nvidia-smi -ac 3505,1410` and forced `--autobatch=off` for isolation.

bench-bot: perf snapshot created: https://internal/bench/1993012345 — warmup 10k tokens, runs x3 per region.

alex: after forcing clocks + autobatch off, eu-west1 p95 dropped to ~45.2ms (within 2% of us-west2). looks like clock governor + batching heuristics interacting with kernel selection. i'll attach full traces to INF-3972 and flag for infra parity checks. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: created INF-3972 — "driver/firmware parity & kernel fallback incidents". assigned to @infra-team.

sara: nice find. follow-ups: (1) add a small startup warmup in the deploy template (10k tokens) to populate KV cache; (2) document recommended `nvidia-smi -ac` profile for A100 in our region rollout guide; (3) add cuBLAS/cuDNN version pin checks to perf CI. :white_check_mark:

mike_g: also add a smoke test that disables autobatch and runs single-stream int8 inference to catch kernel fallbacks early.

alex: yep — will PR the smoke test and attach the kernel traces. thanks everyone!
